findings.label: MED
findings.rationale: SC2.6 (`tests/fleet/e2e/sc2-6-lease-kill.live.test.ts`) did not catch the window by polling. It held it open with a `$SWARMCLAW_FACTORY_FLEET_CLI` wrapper that blocks the `submit` exec. SC2.1 persists the `submitting` entry with its `requestId` before that exec. The same approach works here with no fork code. The factory installs a wrapper that holds `submit` only for the `w:z3-*-code` workId (QA legs pass straight through) and waits on a gate file. The driver polls `state` until `factoryState['z3-code-run']` is `submitting` with a `requestId`, kills the container, releases the gate and restarts. Because the window stays open as long as the wrapper holds, poll cadence and the late arming of `armCrashWindow` no longer matter. Window (b) (submit done, ack not persisted) works the same way with the wrapper holding the exit. I added no production self-kill hook and no new event: the persisted `submitting` entry is already the observation point, and `state` surfaces it verbatim (pinned by test). Freshness (B-3c / B-20) is factory-side: `state.writtenAt` is the fork's own clock at dump time.

findings.label: MED
findings.rationale: Retain traces are now the factory host client's own journaled `retain` calls (`journalingClient`), an observation and no longer a constant. The box half rests on the memgate issuance ledger filtered to write verbs. Per INV-MG that ledger is the only path a box has to bank-write scope: the host Hindsight token is env-only (INV-HM1) and never delivered. A box-env probe would need a new in-box verb (the registry is closed, ADR-1 §2).

findings.label: HIGH
findings.rationale: `cancel <protocolRunId>` runs the existing run-cancel path (`performProtocolRunAction` cancel, which triggers SC2.4 `cancelFactoryRuns`). It also awaits its own `cancelFactoryRuns`, so every outstanding entry is marked cancelled before the process exits. It then runs one awaited, exit-checked `fleet cancel` per outstanding external_job runId, because `cancelFactoryRuns` ignores the exec exit code. Observe entries are excluded per the read-only fence INV-Z2-1. Any non-zero exit is an error. A terminal run is not re-cancelled. A non-z3 or unknown run is refused.

findings.diff_context_ref: src/lib/server/protocols/protocol-z3-exit-round.ts:115 — "the LLM decider is never consulted" is not what the code does
findings.rationale: `processBranchStep` consults the decider whenever no `when` matches, so a case without a `when` cannot act as a catch-all. `z3-branch` now has a third, last case `unmatched` with an always-true condition (`artifact_count_at_least count:0`) that routes to the new step `z3-unmatched`. That step is a branch with no cases and no default: `processBranchStep` throws "had no satisfied path" and the run fails. `defaultDecideBranchCase` returns null for an empty case list before it builds a model (protocol-step-helpers.ts:404), so no LLM is called. The comment is fixed. Tests run the real `processBranchStep` with an unparseable verdict: `z3-branch` takes `unmatched` without calling the decider, `z3-unmatched` rejects, and `defaultDecideBranchCase(run, step, [])` is null. Also mirrored facilitator, observers and goal from `launchProtocolRunForSchedule` into `fireZ3ExitRoundRun`. **Contract delta for the factory: the step-id list gains `z3-unmatched` (11 steps), and `branch_taken.data.caseId` can be `unmatched`.**

findings.diff_context_ref: src/lib/server/runtime/scheduler.ts:503-506 — fire-time throw rejects the whole tick (daemon shutdown)
findings.rationale: Scheduler hook: the literal `'z3_exit_round'` is compared before the lazy import, so no other protocol schedule loads the module. A test pins the literal to the exported constant. The z3 fire is wrapped in try/catch. On refusal it marks the schedule `failed`, adds a history entry (`reason: z3_fire_refused`, with the error in the summary), raises a `schedule_failed` main-loop event, and continues the tick. Test: a tampered row (string `codePollTimeoutMs`) fails only that schedule, and a valid z3 schedule due in the same tick still fires. As a negative control I restored the old hook and the test failed with the refusal error escaping the tick.
